intent: The season finale, in three endings. Each one answers the central question («tu le gardes, tu le partages, ou tu le laisses partir ?»), each has a cost somebody pays, and in each the apartment gives up Odile's letter, which points somewhere else. All three are good endings. None of them is the one where you «lost». Lila leaves in every ending. What the endings change is what she leaves behind. Every ending closes the café question and opens the same season 2 question through a different door: the painting is in your hands, hidden by Gus, or lost in Paris. Season 2 can therefore be written once, with three first episodes.
state_in: Days 58–59 · Thursday 7 and Friday 8 January, the day of Lila's train and the end of Solvel's offer.

Ending 1 · Garder. Requires: evidence_shared = marchand_only · Margaux persuaded in T7 · flat = keep. The cost: Marchand leaves the building he lived in for 41 years. Margaux still carries the café alone. Who «wins» the argument: Gus: everything stays.

Ending 2 · Partager. Requires: the truth made public (fire_photo = wall or evidence_shared = public) · Gus persuaded in T7 · flat = coop. The cost: You give up the flat. Gus loses the café of his childhood as it was. Who «wins» the argument: Marin: it changes so it can survive.
Ending 3 · Laisser partir. Requires: chosen in T7, with Margaux: flat = sell. The cost: The group loses its home. Who «wins» the argument: Lila: nobody holds anybody back.

Each ending runs over two days. Day A · Thursday 7 January: the ending's page, your turn, and at night the apartment yields Odile's letter; the mid-point hook is the letter's last line. Day B · Friday 8 January: the platform at 9:55, then the painting and «À suivre…». Lila leaves in every ending. What the endings change is what she leaves behind.

Ending 1 · What happened in T6/T7: You showed Marchand, and only Marchand, Odile's notebook page: «J'ai demandé à Margaux de mentir. C'est ma faute, pas la sienne.» He withdrew the complaint and renewed Margaux's lease for nine years. To pay for a place in a residence without stairs, he sold his floors above the café to Solvel. He kept the café's walls, so Margaux's rent now pays for his residence. You kept the flat and are moving in. The café stays exactly as it was. The secret stays inside four people.

Ending 2 · What happened in T6/T7: The truth is public: Romy's article, published with your consent, «Le feu du Mistral : une histoire de loyauté». The quartier came. Odile's forty pledges became 212 members of «Le Mistral à nous». Marchand sold the walls to the co-op and not to Solvel, for less, because Odile's notebook had his line: «oui, si Margaux reste». The fire damage was paid from the sale of your flat to the co-op at a low price. The flat is now the co-op's workshop, with painting classes for children in the afternoon, and the meeting room. You rent the little room under the roof from the co-op.

Ending 3 · What happened in T6/T7: In T7, Margaux said the sentence she had never said: «Je veux voir la mer avant d'être vieille. Enfin… plus vieille.» You chose with her to let it go. You sold the flat to Solvel, and the price paid the fire damage and the insurer. Solvel's compensation cleared Margaux's debts. Le Mistral closes tonight. The group loses its home.

The painting above the zinc: a small oil, «Le Mistral sur le canal»: the café's corner in a strong wind, signed «L.». It has hung above the zinc for as long as anyone remembers. All season Lila has had a running line about it: «Pas mal. Mais la lumière est fausse.» The reason is that it was painted from above, from Odile's window.
On the back of the painting (read in ending 1, glimpsed in 2, lost in 3): in ink: «Pour Odile, qui part. — L., 1970»; in pencil, in a shaky recent hand: «Toujours rue de Lancry. — L., 2021».

can_do.en: Say goodbye to a place and to people; read a personal letter.

movements.visual: Morning. Gus on a ladder by the door, screwing up a brass plaque: «LE MISTRAL · DEPUIS 1951». Marin holds the ladder with both hands, as he held the chair in T4.

say.a2: Plus haut ? Plus bas ?

native.en: Higher? Lower?
native.de: Höher? Tiefer?

say.a2: Plus droit.

native.en: Straighter.
native.de: Gerader.

movements.visual: Inside, at the zinc. Margaux and M. Marchand on either side of a nine-year lease. They sign without looking at each other, then they look at each other.

say.a2: Un café ?

native.en: A coffee?
native.de: Einen Kaffee?

say.a2: …Un crème.

native.en: …A café crème.
native.de: …Einen Café crème.

movements.note: A café crème was Odile's order (T4, P3). Nobody remarks on it.

movements.visual: The pavement outside. Movers carry Marchand's furniture past the café window: a dresser, a clock, a framed wedding photograph. A white van with the Solvel logo stands at the kerb. In the café window, Gus's plaque shines.

panel.visual: Marchand on the pavement with the last box, his ring of old keys lighter by two. Camille loads the car behind him (the Camille panel). He turns to Toi.

say.a2: Et vous ? Vous restez ?

native.en: And you? Are you staying?
native.de: Und Sie? Bleiben Sie?

task.en: Tell him whether you're staying, and what Odile's flat is to you now. He is the one who pays for everything staying the same.
task.de: Sag ihm, ob du bleibst und was Odiles Wohnung jetzt für dich ist. Er ist derjenige, der dafür bezahlt, dass alles bleibt, wie es ist.
task.fr: Dis-lui si tu restes, et ce que l'appartement d'Odile est pour toi maintenant. C'est lui qui paie pour que tout reste pareil.

movements.listens_for: Whether the learner is staying, and what Odile's flat is to them now: staying, not knowing, staying for oneself and for him, or sorry that he leaves because of them.

replies.label: Staying, living upstairs
replies.means: The learner is staying: they live upstairs now.
examples: Oui. Je reste. J'habite en haut maintenant.

say.a2: Alors fermez bien la fenêtre de la cuisine. Elle ne ferme pas. Elle n'a jamais fermé.
say.b1: Alors fermez bien la fenêtre de la cuisine. Elle ferme mal. Elle a toujours mal fermé.

native.en: Then close the kitchen window properly. It doesn't close. It never has.
native.de: Dann schließen Sie das Küchenfenster gut. Es schließt nicht. Es hat nie geschlossen.

beats.note: He knows that kitchen. Six years of Sundays.

replies.label: I don't know
replies.means: The learner does not know whether they are staying.

say.a2: Elle non plus, elle ne savait pas. Elle est restée quatorze ans.

native.en: She didn't know either. She stayed fourteen years.
native.de: Sie wusste es auch nicht. Sie ist vierzehn Jahre geblieben.

replies.label: Clumsy but sincere
replies.means: A halting reply: staying for oneself and a little for him, and asking whether he will come on Sundays.
examples: Je reste… pour elle ? Non. Pour moi. Et un peu pour vous. Vous venez le dimanche ?

beats.visual: The «softened» expression, a small reluctant nod.

say.a2: Le dimanche… On verra. Il y a le bus 46.

native.en: Sundays… We'll see. There's the 46 bus.
native.de: Sonntags… Mal sehen. Es gibt den Bus 46.

beats.note: The Sunday lunches pass from Odile to her grandchild. This is the best version of the ending.

examples: Pardon. Vous partez à cause de nous.

say.a2: Non. Je pars à cause de l'escalier.

native.en: No. I'm leaving because of the stairs.
native.de: Nein. Ich gehe wegen der Treppe.

say.a2: Et un peu à cause de vous. Ce n'est pas grave.

native.en: And a little because of you. It's not serious.
native.de: Und ein bisschen wegen Ihnen. Das ist nicht schlimm.

movements.visual: That evening, the booth, exactly as it has always been. Everyone is there: Lila's last evening. Gus stands with his glass raised.

native.de: Nicht heute Abend.

movements.visual: Two in the morning. Margaux alone, counting the till under one lamp. The stool at the end of the zinc, Odile's stool, is empty. This is the cost: nothing changed, including the fact that she carries this alone.

Toi's first night living upstairs. The radiator is cold (the season's oldest joke). Toi kneels and hits it, as Marin taught Toi. Behind the valve, something taped to the wall shifts and slides: an envelope.
Lila on the phone, packing.

say.a2: Lis-le-moi. Tout. Lentement.

native.en: Read it to me. All of it. Slowly.
native.de: Lies ihn mir vor. Alles. Langsam.

movements.note: Friendship path (an open path reads this too). Placed before the letter: she asks to hear it.

movements.visual: Lila came up at midnight to say goodbye and is reading over Toi's shoulder. When Toi reaches «quelqu'un», her hand finds Toi's sleeve.
movements.note: Romance path. Placed after the reading: her hand finds the sleeve at «quelqu'un».

panel.visual: The last line of the letter, alone on the panel: «Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.» Through the floor, the café is dark, and the painting hangs on its nail directly below Toi.
diegetic: Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.

say.a2: Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.

native.en: The painting is right below. Tomorrow morning, Lila leaves. To be continued…

say.b1: Rue de Lancry. C'est à deux cents mètres d'ici.

native.en: I didn't know. That, I didn't know.

panel.visual: Rue de Lancry at dusk. One lit window on a third floor, curtains half-open, an easel visible inside. Toi in the street below, from behind, the painting under one arm.

panel.note: Who remembers what (1). Gus is happiest in this ending, and knows nothing of the notebook. Marin puts his folder in a drawer. He brings it up once, gently, in season 2. Margaux knows you protected her the way she protected Odile. Romy knows there is a story she wasn't given, and she lets it go, once. If `romy.footage = kept`, she gives you the memory card on the platform, without a word. Marchand comes on Sundays if (c).

movements.visual: Gus's hand flat on the new fabric of the booth, where he did his homework as a boy while his mother worked the room.

panel.visual: The Polaroid wall, now permanent and framed. The burnt one hangs in the middle, with a card in Margaux's writing: «Odile Ferrand, 1948–2026. Elle habitait en haut.» Gus sits down stiffly at a long table between two strangers and looks at Toi.

movements.listens_for: Where the learner puts Gus in the changed café: with the group, on the zinc, in himself, or at the bench where his mother worked.

movements.visual: 11 a.m. Margaux on a bench by the canal, doing nothing, her face in the winter sun. The first day off in twenty-five years.
That afternoon, the co-op's builders are tearing out Odile's old kitchen to make the workshop. A builder hands Toi an envelope he found behind the tiles, just above where the stove stood.

panel.note: Gus's mother waited tables at Le Mistral through the 2000s, so she would know. Season 2 can tie Gus's real family to Odile's secret. Who remembers what (2). Gus forgives you by the second week, in his fashion («Tu m'as coûté une banquette»). Marin is sure the co-op was a sign. Margaux is no longer alone, and doesn't know what to do with her hands. Romy's article earns her the Paris contract (seed for season 3). Marchand buys one share. He never comes, but he pays.

say.a2: La lumière est fausse parce qu'il a peint d'en haut. De la fenêtre d'Odile.
say.b1: Je comprends enfin pourquoi la lumière est fausse. Il l'a peint d'en haut. Depuis la fenêtre d'Odile.

native.en: The light is wrong because he painted from above. From Odile's window.
native.de: Das Licht ist falsch, weil er von oben gemalt hat. Von Odiles Fenster aus.

panel.visual: A white van turning out of the quai de Valmy into the city. Through its back window, the corner of a gilt frame.

say.a2: En 1970, quelqu'un a peint le Mistral depuis chez Odile. Aujourd'hui, le tableau est quelque part dans Paris. Lui aussi, peut-être. À suivre…
say.b1: En 1970, quelqu'un a peint le Mistral depuis la fenêtre d'Odile. Le tableau roule quelque part dans Paris. Le peintre aussi, peut-être. À suivre…

native.en: In 1970, someone painted Le Mistral from Odile's place. Today, the painting is somewhere in Paris. So is he, maybe. To be continued…
native.de: 1970 hat jemand den Mistral von Odiles Wohnung aus gemalt. Heute ist das Gemälde irgendwo in Paris. Er vielleicht auch. Fortsetzung folgt…

panel.note: Who remembers what (3). Gus installs the bench in his loft. It is the first true thing in the «château». Marin cries at the neon. Margaux sends you a postcard of the sea with three words: «Elle est grande.» Romy's photo essay on the last night is the best thing she has written. Marchand sends the only Christmas card of his life, to you.

native.en: What is she asking you?
native.de: Worum bittet sie dich?

task.en: Read Odile's letter, alone and in French, and choose what she is asking you.
task.de: Lies Odiles Brief, allein und auf Französisch, und wähle, worum sie dich bittet.
task.fr: Lis la lettre d'Odile, seul(e) et en français, et choisis ce qu'elle te demande.

letter.visual: An envelope, yellowed, addressed in Odile's hand: «Pour toi. Quand tu parleras français.»

document.a2:
Pour toi. Quand tu parleras français.

Je ne t'ai jamais parlé de Paris. Pardon. Paris était trop grand pour l'autre langue.

Ici, j'ai été heureuse deux fois : à vingt ans, et à soixante ans. Entre les deux, j'ai été ta grand-mère. Ce n'était pas moins bien. C'était autre chose.

Maintenant, j'oublie. Alors j'écris.

À Paris, j'ai laissé deux choses : cet appartement, et quelqu'un. L'appartement, tu l'as trouvé.

Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.

Odile
document.b1:
Pour toi. Quand tu parleras français.

Je ne t'ai jamais parlé de Paris, et je te demande pardon. Paris était trop grand pour l'autre langue ; il ne tenait pas dedans.

Ici, j'ai été heureuse deux fois : à vingt ans et à soixante. Entre les deux, j'ai été ta grand-mère, et ce n'était pas moins bien. C'était autre chose.

Je commence à oublier, alors j'écris pendant que je sais encore.

J'ai laissé deux choses à Paris : cet appartement, et quelqu'un. L'appartement, tu l'as trouvé, puisque tu lis ceci.

Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.

Odile

native.en:
For you. When you speak French.

I never told you about Paris. I'm sorry. Paris was too big for the other language.

Here, I was happy twice: at twenty, and at sixty. In between, I was your grandmother. That was no worse. It was something else.

Now I forget. So I write.

In Paris, I left two things: this flat, and someone. The flat, you found.

For the other, look behind the painting of Le Mistral.

Odile
native.de:
Für dich. Wenn du Französisch sprichst.

Ich habe dir nie von Paris erzählt. Verzeih. Paris war zu groß für die andere Sprache.

Hier war ich zweimal glücklich: mit zwanzig und mit sechzig. Dazwischen war ich deine Großmutter. Das war nicht schlechter. Es war etwas anderes.

Jetzt vergesse ich. Also schreibe ich.

In Paris habe ich zwei Dinge zurückgelassen: diese Wohnung und jemanden. Die Wohnung hast du gefunden.

Für das andere schau hinter das Gemälde des Mistral.

Odile

native.en: Sell the flat
native.de: Die Wohnung verkaufen

native.en: Look behind the painting
native.de: Hinter dem Gemälde nachsehen

native.en: Talk to Margaux
native.de: Mit Margaux sprechen

say.a2: Pour l'autre, regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral.

native.en: For the other, look behind the painting of Le Mistral.
native.de: Für das andere schau hinter das Gemälde des Mistral.

nudge.note: Transcription: the script says «If the learner picks wrong, whoever is with them reads the last line aloud. Nothing is lost.» Lila reads it here, in every ending: she is with you on both paths (over your shoulder, on the phone, or holding the table). In ending 2 Marin is in the doorway too. Nothing is lost, nothing is scored.

letter.visual: Toi holding the letter, from behind.
letter.note: This is the payoff of the whole product. The learner reads, alone and in French, a letter written for the day they could. We show no score and no stamp. The next panel is (silence): Toi holding the letter, from behind.

platform.visual: The platform, a long ICE train. The whole group is there. Gus holds up a banner he painted himself, badly, using Lila's T4 banner as a template: «LILA · BERLIN · ON RESTE (ICI)». Marin is already crying. Romy is filming and pretends not to be.

say.a2: On reste ici. Toi, tu pars. C'est clair, non ?
say.b1: Nous, on reste ; toi, tu pars. Le message est limpide.

native.en: We're staying here. You're leaving. That's clear, isn't it?
native.de: Wir bleiben hier. Du gehst. Das ist doch klar, oder?

say.a2: C'est horrible. Je le garde.

native.en: It's horrible. I'm keeping it.
native.de: Das ist schrecklich. Ich behalte es.

platform.visual: Lila hugs Marin. His whole face is in her shoulder. Margaux, a step back, hands Lila a paper bag: a croissant, and a folded Polaroid of the booth.

panel.visual: Toi and Lila, a little apart from the group. The train doors are open. Toi's balloon, empty.

say.a2: Alors. Dernier truc vrai ?
say.b1: Alors. Un dernier truc vrai ?

native.en: So. One last true thing?
native.de: Also. Zum Schluss noch etwas Wahres?

panel.note: Transcription: the path is already decided by now (bible §7): the lines are coloured by it and no reply moves it. An open path reads the friendship lines.

task.en: Your last words to Lila before the train.
task.de: Deine letzten Worte an Lila vor dem Zug.
task.fr: Tes derniers mots à Lila avant le train.

platform.listens_for: Anything: the learner's last words to Lila, however clumsy. She answers whatever is said, directly and first, in the colour of the path. A clumsy but sincere last line is never corrected here.

replies.label: Whatever the learner says
replies.means: Any last words to Lila: she answers what was said, directly and first.

say.a2: Oui. Beaucoup. C'est pour ça que je pars maintenant.

native.en: Yes. A lot. That's why I'm leaving now.
native.de: Ja. Sehr. Deshalb gehe ich jetzt.

beats.note: Transcription: romance path. The script's example: to «Je vais te manquer ?».

say.a2: Évidemment. Je suis géniale.

native.en: Of course. I'm brilliant.
native.de: Natürlich. Ich bin großartig.

beats.note: Transcription: friendship path (an open path reads this too). The script's example: to «Tu vas me manquer.».

replies.label: Clumsy but sincere
replies.means: A halting last line that still says thank you, for the key and for oneself. Never corrected here.
examples: Merci… pour… je sais pas. Pour tout. Pour la clé. Pour moi.

say.a2: "Pour moi." C'est la meilleure.

native.en: "For me." That's the best one.
native.de: "Für mich." Das ist die beste.

say.a2: Tu parles comme Marin, maintenant. C'est grave.

native.en: You talk like Marin now. That's bad.
native.de: Du redest jetzt wie Marin. Das ist schlimm.

platform.visual: She has the copy of the key. She holds it up and puts it in her coat pocket, not in Toi's hand.

say.a2: Je la garde. Pour revenir.
say.b1: Je la garde. Pour pouvoir revenir.

native.en: I'm keeping it. To come back.
native.de: Ich behalte ihn. Um zurückzukommen.

say.a2: On ne se promet rien. On s'écrit.

native.en: We promise each other nothing. We write.
native.de: Wir versprechen uns nichts. Wir schreiben uns.

say.a2: Ton visage, je le finis quand je te revois.

native.en: Your face, I'll finish it when I see you again.
native.de: Dein Gesicht male ich fertig, wenn ich dich wiedersehe.

platform.visual: She presses the key into Toi's palm and closes Toi's fingers over it.

say.a2: Je te la rends. Tu me la redonnes quand je reviens.
say.b1: Je te la rends. Tu me la redonneras à mon retour.

native.en: I'm giving it back to you. You give it back to me when I come back.
native.de: Ich gebe ihn dir zurück. Du gibst ihn mir wieder, wenn ich zurückkomme.

say.a2: Le coin du portrait. Finis-le, toi. Ça va être moche. Parfait.

native.en: The corner of the portrait. You finish it. It's going to be ugly. Perfect.
native.de: Die Ecke des Porträts. Mal du sie fertig. Das wird hässlich. Perfekt.

platform.note: Friendship path (an open path reads this too), without the key.

platform.visual: The doors close. Through the glass, Lila holds up her phone: she wants the photo of the painting's back, or of whatever Toi finds. The train pulls out.

panel.visual: Camille Marchand, about thirty, rooted in the 10th, who has handled the sale for their grandfather. Camille disagrees with Toi, precisely and without contempt.

say.a2: On n'est pas d'accord sur grand-chose, vous et moi.

native.en: We don't agree on much, you and I.
native.de: Wir sind uns in vielen Dingen nicht einig, Sie und ich.

panel.note: Camille uses vous. The switch to tu belongs to season 2. One panel in every ending (seed of the second romantic possibility).

task.en: Answer Camille in your own words.
task.de: Antworte Camille mit deinen eigenen Worten.
task.fr: Réponds à Camille avec tes propres mots.

camille.listens_for: Anything: the learner's line sits between Camille's two lines, and whatever is said, Camille answers with the same closing line.

replies.label: Whatever the learner says
replies.means: Any reply to Camille: agreement, disagreement or a joke.

say.a2: Bien. À la prochaine dispute.

native.en: Good. Until the next dispute.
native.de: Gut. Bis zum nächsten Streit.

Note for the owner. Every ending closes the café question and opens the same season 2 question through a different door: the painting is in your hands, hidden by Gus, or lost in Paris. Season 2 can therefore be written once, with three first episodes.
